  "content": "#include \"sensor_platform.h\"\n#include \"vibration_source.h\"\n#include \"operating_state.h\"\n#include \"app_config.h\"\n#include \"logger.h\"\n\n#include <math.h>\n#include <stdbool.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include \"driver/i2c_master.h\"\n#include \"esp_timer.h\"\n#include \"freertos/FreeRTOS.h\"\n#include \"freertos/task.h\"\n\nstatic const char *TAG = \"sensors\";\nstatic i2c_master_bus_handle_t s_bus;\nstatic i2c_master_dev_handle_t s_mpu;\nstatic i2c_master_dev_handle_t s_pressure;\nstatic bool s_mpu_present;\nstatic bool s_pressure_present;\nstatic bool s_address_present[0x80];\nstatic float s_gravity_x;\nstatic float s_gravity_y;\nstatic float s_gravity_z;\nstatic float s_filtered_magnitude;\nstatic bool s_filter_initialized;\nstatic float s_temperature_c;\nstatic bool s_temperature_valid;\nstatic int16_t s_ac1, s_ac2, s_ac3, s_b1, s_b2, s_mb, s_mc, s_md;\nstatic uint16_t s_ac4, s_ac5, s_ac6;\n\nstatic esp_err_t add_device(uint8_t address, i2c_master_dev_handle_t *device)\n{\n    const i2c_device_config_t config = {\n        .dev_addr_length = I2C_ADDR_BIT_LEN_7,\n        .device_address = address,\n        .scl_speed_hz = APP_I2C_FREQUENCY_HZ,\n    };\n    return i2c_master_bus_add_device(s_bus, &config, device);\n}\n\nstatic esp_err_t read_register(i2c_master_dev_handle_t device, uint8_t reg,\n                               uint8_t *data, size_t length)\n{\n    return i2c_master_transmit_receive(device, &reg, 1, data, length,\n                                        APP_I2C_TIMEOUT_MS);\n}\n\nstatic esp_err_t write_register(uint8_t reg, uint8_t value)\n{\n    uint8_t data[2] = {reg, value};\n    return i2c_master_transmit(s_mpu, data, sizeof(data), APP_I2C_TIMEOUT_MS);\n}\n\nstatic void print_scan(void)\n{\n    ESP_LOGI(TAG, \"I2C scan on SDA=%d SCL=%d\", APP_I2C_SDA_GPIO, APP_I2C_SCL_GPIO);\n    for (uint8_t address = 1; address < 0x7f; ++address) {\n        if (i2c_master_probe(s_bus, address, APP_I2C_TIMEOUT_MS) == ESP_OK) {\n            s_address_present[address] = true;\n            ESP_LOGI(TAG, \"I2C device found at 0x%02X\", address);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nstatic void detect_motion(void)\n{\n    const uint8_t addresses[] = {0x68, 0x69};\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {\n        if (!s_address_present[addresses[i]]) continue;\n        i2c_master_dev_handle_t device = NULL;\n        if (add_device(addresses[i], &device) != ESP_OK) continue;\n        uint8_t id = 0;\n        if (read_register(device, 0x75, &id, 1) == ESP_OK) {\n            ESP_LOGI(TAG, \"motion 0x%02X WHO_AM_I=0x%02X (%s)\", addresses[i], id,\n                     id == 0x68 ? \"MPU-6050\" : \"unknown motion chip\");\n            if (id == 0x68 && !s_mpu_present) {\n                s_mpu = device;\n                s_mpu_present = true;\n                if (write_register(0x6B, 0x00) != ESP_OK ||\n                    write_register(0x1C, 0x00) != ESP_OK ||\n                    write_register(0x1A, APP_MPU_DLPF_CFG) != ESP_OK ||\n                    write_register(0x19, APP_MPU_SAMPLE_RATE_DIV) != ESP_OK) {\n                    ESP_LOGE(TAG, \"MPU-6050 configuration failed\");\n                }\n            } else {\n                i2c_master_bus_rm_device(device);\n            }\n        } else {\n            i2c_master_bus_rm_device(device);\n        }\n    }\n    ESP_LOGI(TAG, \"MPU-6050 detected: %s\", s_mpu_present ? \"yes\" : \"no\");\n}\n\nstatic void detect_pressure(void)\n{\n    const uint8_t addresses[] = {0x76, 0x77};\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {\n        if (!s_address_present[addresses[i]]) continue;\n        i2c_master_dev_handle_t device = NULL;\n        if (add_device(addresses[i], &device) != ESP_OK) continue;\n        uint8_t id = 0;\n        if (read_register(device, 0xD0, &id, 1) == ESP_OK) {\n            const char *name = id == 0x55 ? \"BMP180\" : id == 0x58 ? \"BMP280\" :\n                               id == 0x60 ? \"BME280\" : \"unknown pressure chip\";\n            ESP_LOGI(TAG, \"pressure 0x%02X chip ID=0x%02X (%s)\", addresses[i], id, name);\n            if (id == 0x55 && !s_pressure_present) {\n                s_pressure = device;\n                s_pressure_present = true;\n            } else {\n                i2c_master_bus_rm_device(device);\n            }\n        } else {\n            i2c_master_bus_rm_device(device);\n        }\n    }\n    ESP_LOGI(TAG, \"BMP180 detected: %s\", s_pressure_present ? \"yes\" : \"no\");\n}\n\nstatic void read_bmp180_calibration(void)\n{\n    uint8_t raw[22];\n    if (!s_pressure_present || read_register(s_pressure, 0xAA, raw, sizeof(raw)) != ESP_OK) return;\n    s_ac1 = (int16_t)((raw[0] << 8) | raw[1]); s_ac2 = (int16_t)((raw[2] << 8) | raw[3]);\n    s_ac3 = (int16_t)((raw[4] << 8) | raw[5]); s_ac4 = (uint16_t)((raw[6] << 8) | raw[7]);\n    s_ac5 = (uint16_t)((raw[8] << 8) | raw[9]); s_ac6 = (uint16_t)((raw[10] << 8) | raw[11]);\n    s_b1 = (int16_t)((raw[12] << 8) | raw[13]); s_b2 = (int16_t)((raw[14] << 8) | raw[15]);\n    s_mb = (int16_t)((raw[16] << 8) | raw[17]); s_mc = (int16_t)((raw[18] << 8) | raw[19]);\n    s_md = (int16_t)((raw[20] << 8) | raw[21]);\n}\n\nstatic void update_temperature(void)\n{\n    if (!s_pressure_present) return;\n    uint8_t command[] = {0xF4, 0x2E};\n    if (i2c_master_transmit(s_pressure, command, sizeof(command), APP_I2C_TIMEOUT_MS) != ESP_OK) return;\n    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(5));\n    uint8_t raw[2];\n    if (read_register(s_pressure, 0xF6, raw, sizeof(raw)) != ESP_OK) return;\n    const int32_t ut = (raw[0] << 8) | raw[1];\n    const int32_t x1 = ((ut - s_ac6) * s_ac5) >> 15;\n    const int32_t x2 = (s_mc << 11) / (x1 + s_md);\n    const int32_t b5 = x1 + x2;\n    s_temperature_c = ((float)(b5 + 8) / 16.0f) / 10.0f;\n    s_temperature_valid = isfinite(s_temperature_c);\n}\n\nesp_err_t sensor_platform_init(void)\n{\n    const i2c_master_bus_config_t config = {\n        .i2c_port = I2C_NUM_0, .sda_io_num = APP_I2C_SDA_GPIO, .scl_io_num = APP_I2C_SCL_GPIO,\n        .clk_source = I2C_CLK_SRC_DEFAULT, .glitch_ignore_cnt = 7,\n        .flags.enable_internal_pullup = true,\n    };\n    esp_err_t err = i2c_new_master_bus(&config, &s_bus);\n    if (err != ESP_OK) return err;\n    print_scan(); detect_motion(); detect_pressure(); read_bmp180_calibration();\n    return ESP_OK;\n}\n\nesp_err_t vibration_source_init(void) { return sensor_platform_init(); }\nbool vibration_source_is_present(void) { return s_mpu_present; }\n\nesp_err_t vibration_source_read(vibration_sample_t *sample)\n{\n    if (!sample || !s_mpu_present) return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;\n    uint8_t raw[6];\n    esp_err_t err = read_register(s_mpu, 0x3B, raw, sizeof(raw));\n    if (err != ESP_OK) return err;\n    const int16_t x = (int16_t)((raw[0] << 8) | raw[1]);\n    const int16_t y = (int16_t)((raw[2] << 8) | raw[3]);\n    const int16_t z = (int16_t)((raw[4] << 8) | raw[5]);\n    const float ax = (float)x * APP_MPU_ACCEL_SCALE_G / 32768.0f;\n    const float ay = (float)y * APP_MPU_ACCEL_SCALE_G / 32768.0f;\n    const float az = (float)z * APP_MPU_ACCEL_SCALE_G / 32768.0f;\n    const float gravity_alpha = 0.01f;\n    s_gravity_x += gravity_alpha * (ax - s_gravity_x);\n    s_gravity_y += gravity_alpha * (ay - s_gravity_y);\n    s_gravity_z += gravity_alpha * (az - s_gravity_z);\n    sample->x_g = ax - s_gravity_x; sample->y_g = ay - s_gravity_y; sample->z_g = az - s_gravity_z;\n    sample->magnitude_g = sqrtf(sample->x_g * sample->x_g + sample->y_g * sample->y_g + sample->z_g * sample->z_g);\n    return ESP_OK;\n}\n\nstatic void sensor_task(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    TickType_t last = xTaskGetTickCount();\n    uint32_t sum_squares = 0;\n    float sum_sq = 0.0f, peak = 0.0f;\n    uint32_t count = 0, errors = 0, last_temp_ms = 0;\n    operating_state_init();\n    for (;;) {\n        const uint64_t now_us = esp_timer_get_time();\n        vibration_sample_t sample;\n        if (vibration_source_read(&sample) == ESP_OK && isfinite(sample.magnitude_g)) {\n            if (!s_filter_initialized) { s_filtered_magnitude = sample.magnitude_g; s_filter_initialized = true; }\n            else s_filtered_magnitude = APP_SENSOR_EMA_ALPHA * sample.magnitude_g + (1.0f - APP_SENSOR_EMA_ALPHA) * s_filtered_magnitude;\n            sum_sq += s_filtered_magnitude * s_filtered_magnitude;\n            if (s_filtered_magnitude > peak) peak = s_filtered_magnitude;\n            ++count;\n        } else ++errors;\n        const uint32_t now_ms = (uint32_t)(now_us / 1000ULL);\n        if (now_ms - last_temp_ms >= APP_SENSOR_TEMP_PERIOD_MS) { update_temperature(); last_temp_ms = now_ms; }\n        if (now_ms % APP_SENSOR_WINDOW_MS < APP_SENSOR_RAW_PERIOD_MS && count > 0) {\n            const float rms = sqrtf(sum_sq / (float)count);\n            const sentinel_state_t state = operating_state_update(rms, now_ms);\n            ESP_LOGI(TAG, \"uptime=%lu ms phase=%s vibration_rms=%.3f g peak=%.3f g temp=%s%.2f C samples=%lu errors=%lu\",\n                     (unsigned long)now_ms, operating_state_name(state), rms, peak,\n                     s_temperature_valid ? \"\" : \"invalid \", s_temperature_c,\n                     (unsigned long)count, (unsigned long)errors);\n            sum_sq = 0.0f; peak = 0.0f; count = 0; errors = 0;\n        }\n        vTaskDelayUntil(&last, pdMS_TO_TICKS(APP_SENSOR_RAW_PERIOD_MS));\n    }\n}\n\nvoid sensor_platform_start(void)\n{\n    if (s_mpu_present) xTaskCreate(sensor_task, \"sensor_200hz\", 4096, NULL, 5, NULL);\n    else ESP_LOGW(TAG, \"no supported motion sensor; sensor task not started\");\n}\n"
}

  "path": "C:\\Users\\vishn\\Documents\\projects\\Hackathon\\my_firmware\\craftiai_sentinel\\firmware\\README.md",
  "content": "# CraftiAI Hackathon Sentinel — Phase 1\n\nESP32-C3-DevKitM-1 vibration-monitoring firmware for the HW-290/GY-91 board.\n\n## Hardware\n\n- MPU-6050 and BMP180 on I2C\n- SDA: GPIO4\n- SCL: GPIO5\n- I2C speed: 400 kHz\n- Onboard WS2812 LED: GPIO8 (existing LED behavior preserved)\n- No humidity sensor in this phase; BMP180 does not measure humidity.\n\n## Acquisition and filtering\n\nThe MPU-6050 is configured for 200 Hz raw acquisition using sample-rate divider 4 and DLPF_CFG=2 (approximately 94 Hz accelerometer bandwidth). Samples are read every 5 ms and aggregated into 100 ms windows.\n\nStatic gravity is estimated independently on X/Y/Z and removed before calculating dynamic vibration magnitude. The magnitude is smoothed with the existing EMA:\n\n```text\nfiltered = alpha * new_value + (1 - alpha) * filtered\n```\n\nThe default alpha is `0.25f`. Each 100 ms summary includes RMS vibration, peak vibration, valid sample count, error count, latest BMP180 temperature, and monotonic uptime in milliseconds. Output is approximately 10 Hz rather than raw 200 Hz logging.\n\n## Operating states\n\nThe provisional state machine contains `OFF`, `STARTING`, `RUNNING`, `STOPPING`, and `FAULT`. Startup and shutdown persistence timers prevent normal transients from immediately becoming faults. Defaults are commissioning values and must be replaced or tuned through the later baseline trial:\n\n- Start: 0.08 g RMS\n- Stop: 0.05 g RMS\n- Fault: 0.30 g RMS\n- Recovery: 0.20 g RMS\n- Startup settling: 10 s\n- Stop confirmation: 2 s\n- Fault persistence: 2 s\n- Fault clear persistence: 5 s\n\nThe later phases will add baseline learning, UTC/NTP timestamps, LED anomaly colors, dashboard connectivity, Telegram alerts, and humidity hardware.\n\n## Source boundaries\n\n`interfaces/vibration_source.h` defines the replaceable accelerometer sample contract. `platforms/esp32/sensor_platform.c` owns I2C and sensor-specific acquisition. `services/operating_state.c` owns phase classification. The LED platform remains independent.\n\nAll pins and commissioning values are in `configs/app_config.h`.\n"
}

The next step should be baseline commissioning, but first fix two Phase 1 issues.

1. Correct the effective sampling rate

The log shows:

raw period 5 ms is below the RTOS tick; using one tick (10 ms)

So although the MPU is configured for 200 Hz, the firmware task is currently reading at approximately 100 Hz.

Recommended fix:

  • Use a hardware timer or esp_timer callback to trigger 200 Hz acquisition, or
  • Run the acquisition task at a finer RTOS tick resolution.
  • Keep serial aggregation at 10 Hz.
  • Verify the window sample count is approximately 20 samples per 100 ms.

This matters because vibration features can be distorted when the effective sample rate is lower than intended.

2. Fix startup-state classification

The current output shows the startup transient entering FAULT:

phase=STARTING vibration_rms=0.974 g
phase=FAULT vibration_rms=0.926 g

That is contrary to the requirement that startup and shutdown transients be compensated.

The state machine should prioritize phase context:

OFF → STARTING → RUNNING

During STARTING:

  • Do not enter FAULT immediately.
  • Apply a startup settling timer.
  • Record the startup peak separately.
  • Only enable fault detection after the machine enters RUNNING.

Similarly, during STOPPING, elevated residual vibration should not create a fault.

3. Run the baseline trial

After those fixes, implement a controlled baseline mode.

Collect several normal machine cycles:

  • Machine OFF
  • Startup transient
  • Stable RUNNING
  • Shutdown transient
  • Return to OFF

Record for each window:

  • Timestamp/uptime
  • Operating phase
  • RMS vibration
  • Peak vibration
  • X/Y/Z dynamic values
  • Temperature
  • Sample count
  • Read errors

Recommended initial trial:

  • At least 10 normal cycles
  • Preferably 20–30 cycles
  • Include representative normal loads and operating conditions

4. Generate baseline thresholds

For the stable RUNNING phase, calculate:

  • Mean vibration
  • Standard deviation
  • 95th percentile
  • 99th percentile
  • Normal peak range
  • Per-axis limits
  • Temperature range

Use separate limits for:

  • Startup
  • Stable running
  • Shutdown
  • Machine-off background

Do not continuously learn during an active fault. Baseline updates should be explicitly started and stopped.

5. Add the local anomaly layer

Once the baseline is available:

  • Warning: sustained exceedance of the warning threshold
  • Critical: sustained exceedance of the critical threshold
  • Add hysteresis for recovery
  • Add alert cooldowns
  • Generate one event when an anomaly begins
  • Generate a recovery event when it clears

A useful event structure is:

{
  "uptime_ms": 123456,
  "phase": "RUNNING",
  "severity": "warning",
  "vibration_rms_g": 0.42,
  "vibration_peak_g": 0.71,
  "temperature_c": 26.4,
  "reason": "running vibration exceeded baseline"
}

Recommended order

  1. Fix true 200 Hz acquisition.
  2. Correct startup/shutdown fault suppression.
  3. Add baseline trial mode.
  4. Collect normal machine cycles.
  5. Calculate and validate thresholds.
  6. Add anomaly events and LED status colors.
  7. Add Wi-Fi, NTP timestamps, and MQTT.
  8. Build the web dashboard.
  9. Add Telegram notifications.
  10. Add humidity hardware later, since BMP180 cannot measure humidity.

The immediate technical priority is fixing the 200 Hz acquisition and startup false-fault behavior before collecting baseline data.

# Plan
## Plan
1. Update the existing `craftiai_sentinel` firmware without changing the WS2812 implementation on GPIO8, the I2C pins GPIO4/GPIO5, or the BMP180/MPU identification behavior.
2. Fix the effective 200 Hz acquisition rate by replacing the zero-tick `vTaskDelayUntil()` schedule with a 5 ms `esp_timer` notification schedule. Keep I2C transactions in the sensor task, measure missed notifications, and aggregate approximately 20 samples per 100 ms window.
3. Correct startup and shutdown classification so STARTING and STOPPING transients cannot immediately become FAULT. Fault detection will be active only after RUNNING is established and will require persistence; recovery will use hysteresis and persistence.
4. Add a selectable synthetic vibration source for machine-less testing. Default simulation mode will generate generic OFF, STARTING, RUNNING, and STOPPING profiles with deterministic bounded noise, while retaining the same replaceable `vibration_sample_t` source contract used by the MPU-6050.
5. Add a phase-aware baseline learner. In simulation mode it will automatically collect several complete synthetic cycles; in real-sensor mode it will expose a start/stop learning API for later dashboard or command integration. It will maintain separate OFF, STARTING, RUNNING, and STOPPING statistics, reject incomplete or poor-quality cycles, and persist only validated baselines.
6. Use provisional generic thresholds until a valid baseline exists, then derive running warning and critical limits from learned statistics with safety floors, hysteresis, and configurable persistence. Learned values will never be updated from an active FAULT cycle.
7. Keep BMP180 temperature acquisition at approximately 1 Hz using a non-blocking conversion schedule so the temperature read cannot delay 200 Hz vibration acquisition. Humidity remains out of scope because the installed BMP180 cannot measure it.
8. Add explicit telemetry for uptime, classifier phase, synthetic/real source, vibration RMS and peak, sample counts, missed samples, sensor errors, temperature validity, baseline-learning status, and learned thresholds.
9. Update documentation, build registration, and configuration comments, then run syntax checks, build, flash, and monitor. Verify the simulator completes cycles, the state machine suppresses startup/shutdown false faults, learned values become active, and real-sensor mode remains available.
10. Generate final API documentation after clean runtime verification.

Defaults: simulation mode enabled for the machine-less trial, generic synthetic cycle of OFF 5 s, STARTING 10 s, RUNNING 20 s, and STOPPING 5 s; 200 Hz raw acquisition; 100 ms aggregation windows; bounded deterministic noise; five complete simulated cycles before baseline validation; ten cycles recommended for a real machine; monotonic uptime timestamps; and provisional thresholds retained until the learned baseline passes validation.

**Alternatives:** If `esp_timer` notifications cannot sustain 200 Hz because I2C transactions or task scheduling consume too much time, keep the MPU configured at 200 Hz, reduce logging and contention first, then evaluate a higher-priority acquisition task, a dedicated I2C transaction path, or a measured lower software read rate. If simulation mode prevents physical sensor initialization, continue the synthetic vibration source with temperature marked invalid rather than blocking the trial. If learned statistics are insufficient or contain excessive errors, keep provisional thresholds active and report the baseline as invalid. If NVS persistence is not yet suitable for the baseline blob, retain the validated baseline in RAM for the trial and add versioned NVS storage before field deployment. Do not change GPIO8, GPIO4, or GPIO5, and do not use restricted GPIO11-GPIO17.

I’ll update the existing craftiai_sentinel firmware with two operating modes.

1. Real sensor mode

  • RUNNING: 20 seconds, approximately 0.05 g RMS with 0.01 g bounded noise
  • STOPPING: 5 seconds, transient up to approximately 0.40 g

The simulation will use the same vibrationsamplet interface as the MPU-6050 so it can be replaced without changing the filtering, state, baseline, or future anomaly logic.

3. State-machine fixes

Startup and shutdown transients will not immediately become faults.

  "content": "#include \"baseline_learner.h\"\n#include <float.h>\n\nstatic baseline_phase_stats_t s_stats[5];\nstatic uint32_t s_required_cycles;\nstatic uint32_t s_cycles;\nstatic bool s_valid;\n\nvoid baseline_learner_init(uint32_t required_cycles)\n{\n    s_required_cycles = required_cycles;\n    s_cycles = 0;\n    s_valid = false;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < 5; ++i) {\n        s_stats[i].mean_g = 0.0f;\n        s_stats[i].min_g = FLT_MAX;\n        s_stats[i].max_g = 0.0f;\n        s_stats[i].windows = 0;\n    }\n}\n\nvoid baseline_learner_observe(sentinel_state_t state, float rms_g)\n{\n    if (s_valid || state < SENTINEL_STATE_OFF || state > SENTINEL_STATE_FAULT) return;\n    baseline_phase_stats_t *stats = &s_stats[state];\n    ++stats->windows;\n    stats->mean_g += (rms_g - stats->mean_g) / (float)stats->windows;\n    if (rms_g < stats->min_g) stats->min_g = rms_g;\n    if (rms_g > stats->max_g) stats->max_g = rms_g;\n}\n\nvoid baseline_learner_cycle_complete(void)\n{\n    if (!s_valid && ++s_cycles >= s_required_cycles) s_valid = true;\n}\n\nbool baseline_learner_is_valid(void) { return s_valid; }\nuint32_t baseline_learner_cycles(void) { return s_cycles; }\nconst baseline_phase_stats_t *baseline_learner_stats(sentinel_state_t state)\n{\n    return (state >= SENTINEL_STATE_OFF && state <= SENTINEL_STATE_FAULT) ? &s_stats[state] : NULL;\n}\n"

{
  "path": "C:\\Users\\vishn\\Documents\\projects\\Hackathon\\my_firmware\\craftiai_sentinel\\firmware\\docs\\overview.md",
  "content": "# CraftiAI Hackathon Sentinel — machine-less commissioning\n\nPhase 1 now supports a synthetic vibration source for development without a machine, while retaining the real MPU-6050 path for deployment.\n\n## Hardware and preserved paths\n\n- MPU-6050/BMP180 I2C: SDA GPIO4, SCL GPIO5\n- WS2812 LED: GPIO8; the existing LED implementation is unchanged\n- Humidity is not measured because BMP180 has no humidity channel\n\n## Simulation and baseline\n\n`APP_SENSOR_SIMULATION` is enabled by default for the machine-less trial. It generates repeating generic OFF, STARTING, RUNNING, and STOPPING profiles with configurable durations. The same vibration sample contract is used for simulation and the real sensor.\n\nThe phase-aware baseline learner maintains per-phase mean, minimum, maximum, and window counts. It reports learning progress and becomes valid after the configured number of complete commissioning cycles. These synthetic values are for software validation only and must not be used as machine acceptance limits.\n\n## Telemetry and states\n\nTelemetry includes uptime, phase, vibration RMS and peak, temperature validity, sample/error counters, and baseline status. Startup/shutdown transients are not immediately classified as faults. The states are OFF, STARTING, RUNNING, STOPPING, and FAULT.\n\nBefore field deployment, disable simulation, collect at least 10–30 complete normal machine cycles, validate the learned baseline, and then tune anomaly thresholds from real data.\n"
}

- ## Operating states
+ The phase-aware baseline learner maintains per-phase mean, minimum, maximum, and window counts. It reports learning progress and becomes valid after the configured number of complete commissioning cycles. These synthetic values are for software validation only and must not be used as machine acceptance limits.
📄 edit: \\?\C:\Users\vishn\Documents\projects\Hackathon\my_firmware\craftiai_sentinel\firmware\docs\overview.md (L19–20)
- The provisional classifier provides OFF, STARTING, RUNNING, STOPPING, and FAULT states. Persistence and hysteresis settings prevent immediate classification of ordinary startup and shutdown transients as faults. Thresholds are commissioning values and should be replaced after the baseline trial.
+ ## Telemetry and states
📄 edit: \\?\C:\Users\vishn\Documents\projects\Hackathon\my_firmware\craftiai_sentinel\firmware\docs\overview.md (L21–22)
- ## Scope boundary
+ Telemetry includes uptime, phase, vibration RMS and peak, temperature validity, sample/error counters, and baseline status. Startup/shutdown transients are not immediately classified as faults. The states are OFF, STARTING, RUNNING, STOPPING, and FAULT.
📄 edit: \\?\C:\Users\vishn\Documents\projects\Hackathon\my_firmware\craftiai_sentinel\firmware\docs\overview.md (L23–32)
- This phase establishes reliable phase-tagged sensor telemetry. Humidity hardware, baseline learning, UTC/NTP timestamps, LED anomaly patterns, dashboard connectivity, and Telegram alerts are deferred to subsequent phases.
- ## Modules
- - `interfaces/vibration_source.h`: replaceable accelerometer sample contract.
- - `platforms/esp32/sensor_platform.c`: I2C, MPU-6050, BMP180, filtering, and telemetry windows.
- - `services/operating_state.c`: operating-state classification.
- - `platforms/esp32/led_platform.c`: independent GPIO8 WS2812 implementation.
- - `configs/app_config.h`: acquisition, filter, and state parameters.
+ Before field deployment, disable simulation, collect at least 10–30 complete normal machine cycles, validate the learned baseline, and then tune anomaly thresholds from real data.

The state classifier suppresses startup/shutdown false faults. A phase-aware learner records per-phase mean/min/max/window counts and reports learning progress. Synthetic baselines validate software behavior only; they are not machine acceptance limits.\n\n## Hardware path\n\nReal mode retains the MPU-6050 and BMP180 on I2C SDA GPIO4/SCL GPIO5, with the WS2812 LED on GPIO8. Disable simulation before field installation and collect at least 10–30 complete normal machine cycles before enabling learned thresholds. BMP180 temperature is available; humidity remains unsupported because BMP180 has no humidity channel.\n\n## Telemetry\n\nOutput includes uptime, phase, vibration RMS/peak, temperature validity, sample/error counts, and baseline status/cycle count. The next phases add real-machine baseline controls, persistent baseline storage, anomaly events, LED alert mapping, network synchronization, dashboard, and Telegram notifications.\n"
}

# Plan
## Plan
1. Correct the baseline learner so a cycle is counted only after the ordered sequence `OFF → STARTING → RUNNING → STOPPING → OFF` completes without entering `FAULT`.
2. Improve simulator and acquisition bookkeeping for deterministic 200 Hz sampling, 100 ms windows, missed-notification reporting, and phase-aware baseline statistics.
3. Run the simulator continuously for at least 210 seconds, allowing the configured five 40-second cycles to complete, and verify that the learner reaches `baseline=valid cycles=5`.
4. Record the learned synthetic values for OFF, STARTING, RUNNING, and STOPPING, including mean, minimum, maximum, sample/window counts, and standard deviation where available. Mark these values as test-only and do not use them as production machine thresholds.
5. Disable simulation mode in the firmware configuration, disable automatic real-mode learning until an explicit commissioning command exists, rebuild, flash, and verify MPU-6050/BMP180 real-sensor operation on the existing hardware.
6. Confirm that real mode has no simulator log messages, preserves the 200 Hz timer-driven acquisition path, reports missed samples and I2C errors, keeps startup/shutdown transients out of `FAULT`, and does not change GPIO8 LED or GPIO4/GPIO5 wiring.
7. Update the project documentation and regenerate Doxygen after both simulator learning and real-sensor verification. The next phase can then implement persistent, user-triggered real-machine baseline commissioning and anomaly thresholds.

Defaults: five complete simulated cycles, 40 seconds per cycle, approximately 210 seconds of simulator runtime, deterministic generic profiles, no synthetic baseline persistence, `APP_SENSOR_SIMULATION=0` after the trial, automatic baseline learning disabled in real mode, monotonic uptime timestamps, and humidity remaining out of scope.

The synthetic baseline is only a pipeline and state-machine validation artifact. It must be discarded on the transition to real mode and must not trigger production alerts or define thresholds for an actual machine.

**Alternatives:** If the learner does not reach five valid cycles, inspect the logged phase transitions and extend the monitor duration rather than accepting partial data. If synthetic STARTING or STOPPING data still reaches FAULT, fix state-transition precedence and persistence before collecting the baseline again. If missed notifications or I2C latency prevent approximately 20 samples per window, retain the MPU configuration but reduce work in the acquisition task and defer advanced FIFO/interrupt handling to the next phase. If real hardware is absent or unreadable after simulation is disabled, keep the device in real mode with sensor health marked invalid; do not silently fall back to simulation. If the synthetic baseline needs to be retained for regression tests, store it separately as test metadata, never as the active production baseline.

Next planned phase: real-machine commissioning

The simulator has been stopped and the firmware is back in real-sensor mode. The next phase should add a controlled baseline workflow for a real machine.

Phase 2 — Baseline commissioning

Implement:

  1. Explicit baseline commands

- STARTBASELINE - STOPBASELINE - RESETBASELINE - BASELINESTATUS

  1. Real-machine cycle learning

- Learn separate profiles for: - OFF - STARTING - RUNNING - STOPPING - Require complete, ordered cycles. - Reject cycles with sensor errors or unexpected FAULT states. - Recommend collecting at least 10 cycles, preferably 20–30.

  1. Persistent baseline storage

- Store validated baseline data in NVS. - Include: - Firmware/schema version - Device ID - Cycle count - Per-phase statistics - Timestamp or generation number - Never overwrite a valid baseline with incomplete or faulty data.

  1. Learned anomaly thresholds

- Derive warning and critical thresholds from the stable RUNNING profile. - Use persistence timers and hysteresis. - Keep startup and shutdown thresholds separate so their normal transients are not reported as faults.

  1. Anomaly event model

- Create one event when an anomaly starts. - Include: - Uptime timestamp - Phase - Severity - RMS and peak vibration - Temperature - Baseline threshold - Reason - Create a recovery event when the signal returns to normal.

Then Phase 3 — Local alerting

Use the GPIO8 WS2812 LED to show state:

  • Green: normal running
  • Blue: booting/connecting
  • Yellow: baseline collection or warning
  • Red: critical vibration anomaly
  • Purple: sensor fault
  • Off: machine OFF

The current LED driver should remain isolated; only a state-to-color service should be added.

Then Phase 4 — Time and connectivity

Add:

  • Wi-Fi station mode
  • NTP synchronization
  • UTC timestamps alongside uptime
  • MQTT over TLS
  • Telemetry publishing
  • Anomaly event publishing
  • Remote configuration commands

Then Phase 5 — Backend and notifications

Build:

  • MQTT ingestion service
  • Time-series storage
  • Device registry
  • Anomaly database
  • Web dashboard
  • Telegram alert bot

The BMP180 still cannot provide humidity. Humidity support remains a hardware decision for a later phase.

Important correction

The simulator was run and then disabled, but the available console excerpt did not show a definitive baseline=valid cycles=5 marker. Therefore, its output should be treated as a software exercise, not a validated baseline. That is acceptable because simulated values must not become production thresholds.

The immediate next implementation should be:

Add explicit real-machine baseline start/stop/status commands with persistent NVS storage and validation.

# Plan
## Phase 2 and 3 plan — real-machine commissioning and local alerting

1. Keep the device in real-sensor mode with simulation disabled. Preserve MPU-6050 at I2C `0x68`, BMP180 at `0x77`, I2C on GPIO4/GPIO5, WS2812 on GPIO8, and use the board UART console on RX GPIO20/TX GPIO21 for commands.
2. Replace compile-time-only learning with a runtime commissioning workflow controlled by serial commands: `START_BASELINE`, `STOP_BASELINE`, `RESET_BASELINE`, `BASELINE_STATUS`, and `HELP`.
3. Require 10 complete ordered cycles: `OFF → STARTING → RUNNING → STOPPING → OFF`. A cycle is invalidated by `FAULT`, unexpected phase ordering, excessive missed samples, or insufficient valid vibration windows. A command issued during another phase waits for a clean OFF phase before beginning a candidate baseline.
4. Maintain separate per-phase statistics for vibration RMS and peak, including count, mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, and quality counters. Record valid temperature statistics when available, but do not prevent vibration baseline completion if temperature is temporarily unavailable.
5. Keep the previous validated baseline active while a new candidate is being collected. Commit a candidate only after 10 valid cycles pass validation; incomplete or invalid candidates are discarded without overwriting the previous baseline.
6. Store validated baselines in versioned, CRC-protected, two-slot NVS records with a generation number, schema version, cycle count, source metadata, statistics, and derived thresholds. Load and validate the newest record at boot; reject corrupt, incompatible, or partial records safely.
7. Derive running vibration warning and critical thresholds from the validated RUNNING profile using mean plus 3 standard deviations and mean plus 5 standard deviations, respectively, with safety floors of `0.08 g RMS` and `0.30 g RMS`. Enforce finite values and a positive critical-over-warning margin. No vibration anomaly alert is armed until a valid baseline exists.
8. Add persistent anomaly detection with hysteresis. Evaluate vibration anomalies only in RUNNING, require a default 2-second persistence period, emit one start event per anomaly, optionally emit reminders no more often than every 5 minutes, and emit a recovery event after 5 seconds below the recovery threshold. STARTING and STOPPING transients must never generate vibration faults.
9. Add local WS2812 status indication without changing GPIO8 or the existing led_strip component: OFF is LED off, STARTING/STOPPING are blue, normal RUNNING is green, baseline collection is yellow, warning is amber/yellow, critical anomaly is red, and sensor-health failure is purple. Use deterministic priority: sensor fault, critical anomaly, warning, baseline mode, operating phase.
10. Route all baseline and anomaly operations through the sensor/control task or a queue so the serial parser cannot mutate learner state concurrently with 200 Hz acquisition. Keep command parsing line-buffered and bounded, tolerate CR/LF input, reject unknown or overlong commands, and return machine-readable status through the serial console.
11. Preserve 200 Hz acquisition and 100 ms aggregation. Report valid samples, missed timer notifications, I2C errors, temperature validity, baseline state, cycle count, active thresholds, operating phase, RMS, peak, and anomaly severity. Do not use simulated values as production baseline data.
12. Update documentation and configuration comments with command syntax, 10-cycle acceptance rules, NVS schema behavior, threshold formulas, LED priority, timestamp semantics, and the fact that humidity remains unsupported because BMP180 has no humidity sensor.
13. Run syntax checks and a full build, flash the firmware, verify command behavior and persistence across reboot, exercise invalid and interrupted commissioning runs, confirm the LED mappings, and regenerate Doxygen only after runtime verification succeeds.

Defaults: simulation disabled (`APP_SENSOR_SIMULATION=0`), 10 required complete cycles, 95% minimum valid vibration-window quality per candidate phase, no FAULT states during an accepted cycle, 2-second anomaly persistence, 5-second recovery persistence, 5-minute reminder interval, monotonic uptime timestamps until NTP is introduced, and no temperature anomaly thresholds until machine-specific environmental limits are commissioned.

No clarifying questions are needed because the command transport, validation count, and LED color mapping were already specified.

**Alternatives:** If the UART command path is unavailable on the current monitor connection, expose the same bounded parser through the existing ESP-IDF console/USB-JTAG console without changing the command protocol. If NVS space or atomic blob writes are insufficient, keep the same versioned CRC record format but use two fixed NVS keys or a small dedicated data partition. If 200 Hz I2C acquisition loses notifications during NVS commits or LED updates, keep NVS and LED work off the acquisition path, reduce logging, and use an acquisition queue or MPU FIFO before lowering the configured sample rate. If a real-machine candidate cannot complete 10 valid cycles, retain the prior validated baseline, report the rejection reason, and do not arm anomaly alerts. If learned variance is zero or non-finite, use the configured safety floors and mark the baseline as requiring review rather than accepting unsafe thresholds.

  • Temperature statistics where available

Keep the previous valid baseline active while a new candidate is being collected. Only commit a new baseline after 10 cycles pass validation.

Persist accepted baselines in versioned, CRC-protected, two-slot NVS storage.

Thresholds

For stable RUNNING vibration:

warning  = mean + 3 × standard deviation
critical = mean + 5 × standard deviation

With safety floors:

  • Warning minimum: 0.08 g RMS
  • Critical minimum: 0.30 g RMS

Anomaly detection will only be active during RUNNING.

  • Anomaly persistence: 2 seconds
  • Recovery persistence: 5 seconds
  • Reminder interval: 5 minutes
  • No alerts from STARTING or STOPPING transients
  • No anomaly alert until a valid baseline exists

Phase 3 — Local LED alerts

LED priority:

  1. Sensor fault: purple
  2. Critical anomaly: red
  3. Warning: amber/yellow
  4. Baseline collection: yellow
  5. Operating phase:

- OFF: off - STARTING/STOPPING: blue - Normal RUNNING: green

The existing GPIO8 LED driver remains isolated and unchanged at the hardware level.

Runtime safety

  • Serial commands are line-buffered and bounded.
  • Commands are passed to the sensor/control task rather than modifying acquisition state directly.
  • Acquisition remains at 200 Hz with 100 ms aggregation.
  • NVS writes and LED updates stay off the acquisition path.
  • Telemetry includes timestamps, phase, RMS/peak, sample quality, errors, baseline state, thresholds, and anomaly severity.
  • Humidity remains unsupported because BMP180 has no humidity channel.

After implementation, I’ll build, flash, exercise the commands and LED behavior, verify baseline persistence across reboot, test invalid commissioning runs, and regenerate documentation.

// ===== C:/Espressif/esp-idf-release-v5.5/components/nvs_flash/include/nvs_flash.h =====
/*
 * SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2015-2023 Espressif Systems (Shanghai) CO LTD
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */
#ifndef nvs_flash_h
#define nvs_flash_h

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#include "nvs.h"
#include "esp_partition.h"


#define NVS_KEY_SIZE 32 // AES-256

/**
 * @brief Key for encryption and decryption
 */
typedef struct {
    uint8_t eky[NVS_KEY_SIZE]; /*!<  XTS encryption and decryption key*/
    uint8_t tky[NVS_KEY_SIZE]; /*!<  XTS tweak key */
} nvs_sec_cfg_t;

/**
 * @brief Callback function prototype for generating the NVS encryption keys
 */
typedef esp_err_t (*nvs_flash_generate_keys_t) (const void *scheme_data, nvs_sec_cfg_t* cfg);

/**
 * @brief Callback function prototype for reading the NVS encryption keys
 */
typedef esp_err_t (*nvs_flash_read_cfg_t) (const void *scheme_data, nvs_sec_cfg_t* cfg);

/**
 * @brief NVS encryption: Security scheme configuration structure
 */
typedef struct
{
    int scheme_id;                                /*!<  Security Scheme ID (E.g. HMAC) */
    void *scheme_data;                            /*!<  Scheme-specific data (E.g. eFuse block for HMAC-based key generation) */
    nvs_flash_generate_keys_t nvs_flash_key_gen;  /*!<  Callback for the nvs_flash_key_gen implementation */
    nvs_flash_read_cfg_t nvs_flash_read_cfg;      /*!<  Callback for the nvs_flash_read_keys implementation */
} nvs_sec_scheme_t;

/**
 * @brief Initialize the default NVS partition.
 *
 * This API initialises the default NVS partition. The default NVS partition
 * is the one that is labeled "nvs" in the partition table.
 *
 * When "NVS_ENCRYPTION" is enabled in the menuconfig, this API enables
 * the NVS encryption for the default NVS partition as follows
 *      1. Read security configurations from the first NVS key
 *         partition listed in the partition table. (NVS key partition is
 *         any "data" type partition which has the subtype value set to "nvs_keys")
 *      2. If the NVS key partition obtained in the previous step is empty,
 *         generate and store new keys in that NVS key partition.
 *      3. Internally call "nvs_flash_secure_init()" with
 *         the security configurations obtained/generated in the previous steps.
 *
 * Post initialization NVS read/write APIs
 * remain the same irrespective of NVS encryption.
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK if storage was successfully initialized.
 *      - ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES if the NVS storage contains no empty pages
 *        (which may happen if NVS partition was truncated)
 *      - ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND if no partition with label "nvs" is found in the partition table
 *      - ESP_ERR_NO_MEM in case memory could not be allocated for the internal structures
 *      - one of the error codes from the underlying flash storage driver
 *      - error codes from nvs_flash_read_security_cfg API (when "NVS_ENCRYPTION" is enabled).
 *      - error codes from nvs_flash_generate_keys API (when "NVS_ENCRYPTION" is enabled).
 *      - error codes from nvs_flash_secure_init_partition API (when "NVS_ENCRYPTION" is enabled) .
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_init(void);

/**
 * @brief Initialize NVS flash storage for the specified partition.
 *
 * @param[in]  partition_label   Label of the partition. Must be no longer than 16 characters.
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK if storage was successfully initialized.
 *      - ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES if the NVS storage contains no empty pages
 *        (which may happen if NVS partition was truncated)
 *      - ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND if specified partition is not found in the partition table
 *      - ESP_ERR_NO_MEM in case memory could not be allocated for the internal structures
 *      - one of the error codes from the underlying flash storage driver
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_init_partition(const char *partition_label);

/**
 * @brief Initialize NVS flash storage for the partition specified by partition pointer.
 *
 * @param[in] partition pointer to a partition obtained by the ESP partition API.
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK if storage was successfully initialized
 *      - ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES if the NVS storage contains no empty pages
 *        (which may happen if NVS partition was truncated)
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG in case partition is NULL
 *      - ESP_ERR_NO_MEM in case memory could not be allocated for the internal structures
 *      - one of the error codes from the underlying flash storage driver
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_init_partition_ptr(const esp_partition_t *partition);

/**
 * @brief Deinitialize NVS storage for the default NVS partition
 *
 * Default NVS partition is the partition with "nvs" label in the partition table.
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK on success (storage was deinitialized)
 *      - ESP_ERR_NVS_NOT_INITIALIZED if the storage was not initialized prior to this call
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_deinit(void);

/**
 * @brief Deinitialize NVS storage for the given NVS partition
 *
 * @param[in]  partition_label   Label of the partition
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK on success
 *      - ESP_ERR_NVS_NOT_INITIALIZED if the storage for given partition was not
 *        initialized prior to this call
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_deinit_partition(const char* partition_label);

/**
 * @brief Erase the default NVS partition
 *
 * Erases all contents of the default NVS partition (one with label "nvs").
 *
 * @note If the partition is initialized, this function first de-initializes it. Afterwards, the partition has to
 *       be initialized again to be used.
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK on success
 *      - ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND if there is no NVS partition labeled "nvs" in the
 *        partition table
 *      - different error in case de-initialization fails (shouldn't happen)
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_erase(void);

/**
 * @brief Erase specified NVS partition
 *
 * Erase all content of a specified NVS partition
 *
 * @note If the partition is initialized, this function first de-initializes it. Afterwards, the partition has to
 *       be initialized again to be used.
 *
 * @param[in]  part_name    Name (label) of the partition which should be erased
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK on success
 *      - ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND if there is no NVS partition with the specified name
 *        in the partition table
 *      - different error in case de-initialization fails (shouldn't happen)
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_erase_partition(const char *part_name);

/**
 * @brief Erase custom partition.
 *
 * Erase all content of specified custom partition.
 *
 * @note
 *  If the partition is initialized, this function first de-initializes it.
 *  Afterwards, the partition has to be initialized again to be used.
 *
 * @param[in] partition pointer to a partition obtained by the ESP partition API.
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK on success
 *      - ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND if there is no partition with the specified
 *        parameters in the partition table
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG in case partition is NULL
 *      - one of the error codes from the underlying flash storage driver
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_erase_partition_ptr(const esp_partition_t *partition);

/**
 * @brief Initialize the default NVS partition.
 *
 * This API initialises the default NVS partition. The default NVS partition
 * is the one that is labeled "nvs" in the partition table.
 *
 * @param[in]  cfg Security configuration (keys) to be used for NVS encryption/decryption.
 *                              If cfg is NULL, no encryption is used.
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK if storage has been initialized successfully.
 *      - ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES if the NVS storage contains no empty pages
 *        (which may happen if NVS partition was truncated)
 *      - ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND if no partition with label "nvs" is found in the partition table
 *      - ESP_ERR_NO_MEM in case memory could not be allocated for the internal structures
 *      - one of the error codes from the underlying flash storage driver
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_secure_init(nvs_sec_cfg_t* cfg);

/**
 * @brief Initialize NVS flash storage for the specified partition.
 *
 * @param[in]  partition_label   Label of the partition. Note that internally, a reference to
 *                               passed value is kept and it should be accessible for future operations
 *
 * @param[in]  cfg Security configuration (keys) to be used for NVS encryption/decryption.
 *                              If cfg is null, no encryption/decryption is used.
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK if storage has been initialized successfully.
 *      - ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES if the NVS storage contains no empty pages
 *        (which may happen if NVS partition was truncated)
 *      - ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND if specified partition is not found in the partition table
 *      - ESP_ERR_NO_MEM in case memory could not be allocated for the internal structures
 *      - one of the error codes from the underlying flash storage driver
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_secure_init_partition(const char *partition_label, nvs_sec_cfg_t* cfg);

/**
 * @brief Generate and store NVS keys in the provided esp partition
 *
 * @param[in]  partition Pointer to partition structure obtained using
 *                       esp_partition_find_first or esp_partition_get.
 *                       Must be non-NULL.
 * @param[out] cfg       Pointer to nvs security configuration structure.
 *                       Pointer must be non-NULL.
 *                       Generated keys will be populated in this structure.
 *
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK, if cfg was read successfully;
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG, if partition or cfg is NULL;
 *      - or error codes from esp_partition_write/erase APIs.
 */

esp_err_t nvs_flash_generate_keys(const esp_partition_t* partition, nvs_sec_cfg_t* cfg);


/**
 * @brief Read NVS security configuration from a partition.
 *
 * @param[in]  partition Pointer to partition structure obtained using
 *                       esp_partition_find_first or esp_partition_get.
 *                       Must be non-NULL.
 * @param[out] cfg       Pointer to nvs security configuration structure.
 *                       Pointer must be non-NULL.
 *
 * @note  Provided partition is assumed to be marked 'encrypted'.
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK, if cfg was read successfully;
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG, if partition or cfg is NULL
 *      - ESP_ERR_NVS_KEYS_NOT_INITIALIZED, if the partition is not yet written with keys.
 *      - ESP_ERR_NVS_CORRUPT_KEY_PART, if the partition containing keys is found to be corrupt
 *      - or error codes from esp_partition_read API.
 */

esp_err_t nvs_flash_read_security_cfg(const esp_partition_t* partition, nvs_sec_cfg_t* cfg);

/**
 * @brief Registers the given security scheme for NVS encryption
 *        The scheme registered with sec_scheme_id by this API be used as
 *        the default security scheme for the "nvs" partition.
 *        Users will have to call this API explicitly in their application.
 *
 * @param[in] scheme_cfg  Pointer to the security scheme configuration structure
 *                        that the user (or the nvs_key_provider) wants to register.
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK, if security scheme registration succeeds;
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG, if scheme_cfg is NULL;
 *      - ESP_FAIL, if security scheme registration fails
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_register_security_scheme(nvs_sec_scheme_t *scheme_cfg);

/**
 * @brief   Fetch the configuration structure for the default active
 *          security scheme for NVS encryption
 *
 * @return  Pointer to the default active security scheme configuration
 *          (NULL if no scheme is registered yet i.e. active)
 */
nvs_sec_scheme_t *nvs_flash_get_default_security_scheme(void);

/**
 * @brief Generate (and store) the NVS keys using the specified key-protection scheme
 *
 * @param[in] scheme_cfg   Security scheme specific configuration
 *
 * @param[out] cfg         Security configuration (encryption keys)
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK, if cfg was populated successfully with generated encryption keys;
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG, if scheme_cfg or cfg is NULL;
 *      - ESP_FAIL, if the key generation process fails
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_generate_keys_v2(nvs_sec_scheme_t *scheme_cfg, nvs_sec_cfg_t* cfg);

/**
 * @brief Read NVS security configuration set by the specified security scheme
 *
 * @param[in] scheme_cfg   Security scheme specific configuration
 *
 * @param[out] cfg         Security configuration (encryption keys)
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK, if cfg was read successfully;
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG, if scheme_cfg or cfg is NULL;
 *      - ESP_FAIL, if the key reading process fails
 */
esp_err_t nvs_flash_read_security_cfg_v2(nvs_sec_scheme_t *scheme_cfg, nvs_sec_cfg_t* cfg);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif


#endif /* nvs_flash_h */

# Plan
## Plan
1. Complete the partially implemented Phase 2/3 control path. The current serial parser only logs accepted commands, its queue is unused, and learning is disabled by `APP_SENSOR_LEARNING_ENABLE=0`; both serial and dashboard controls will use one bounded command bus.
2. Implement the real-machine baseline workflow with 10 complete ordered cycles: `OFF → STARTING → RUNNING → STOPPING → OFF`. Track per-phase RMS/peak statistics, quality counters, invalidation reasons, and candidate-versus-active baseline state.
3. Persist only validated baselines using versioned, CRC-protected records and atomic two-slot storage. The active baseline must survive reboot and must never be overwritten by an incomplete or invalid commissioning run.
4. Integrate learner observation, telemetry snapshots, anomaly detection, and command handling without blocking the 200 Hz acquisition path. Use 2-second anomaly persistence, 5-second recovery persistence, hysteresis, and no anomaly evaluation outside `RUNNING`.
5. Integrate the existing GPIO8 WS2812 driver with the requested priority: sensor fault purple, critical anomaly red, warning amber, baseline collection yellow, STARTING/STOPPING blue, normal RUNNING green, and OFF off.
6. Add a device-hosted dashboard using ESP-IDF's native HTTP server and embedded browser assets. FastAPI cannot run on the ESP32-C3; provide the same REST contract through a host-side FastAPI reference/proxy for development only, while the production dashboard is served directly by the device.
7. Use a local WPA2 SoftAP by default so the dashboard works without an external machine network. Derive the SSID from the device identity, keep the password/API token out of source control, and expose state-changing operations only through authenticated POST endpoints. Poll telemetry from the browser at 1 Hz using bounded responses and a small in-RAM history buffer.
8. Validate both control paths, invalid commands, baseline interruption, NVS recovery, dashboard authentication, LED priority, telemetry quality, and reboot behavior. Use a temporary test-only simulator or fixture if needed, then leave production configuration in real-sensor mode with simulation disabled.
9. Update documentation and regenerate Doxygen only after syntax checks, build, device verification, and dashboard checks pass.

Defaults: 10-cycle validation; at least 95% valid windows per candidate phase; monotonic uptime timestamps; warning threshold `max(0.08 g, mean + 3σ)`; critical threshold `max(0.30 g, mean + 5σ)` with a positive critical margin; 2-second anomaly persistence; 5-second recovery persistence; 5-minute reminder interval; 1-second dashboard polling; 120 retained telemetry points; bounded command and HTTP bodies; local WPA2 SoftAP with generated credentials; and no temperature anomaly thresholds until explicitly commissioned. No GPIO assignments change: GPIO4/GPIO5 remain I2C, GPIO8 remains WS2812, and restricted GPIO11–GPIO17 remain unused.

The requested FastAPI stack is treated as a compatibility/reference layer rather than firmware runtime code because Python/FastAPI cannot be deployed on this 4 MB, no-PSRAM ESP32-C3 target.

**Alternatives:** If the ESP32-C3 cannot sustain the dashboard service alongside acquisition, keep the native REST API minimal, reduce telemetry history and logging, and move only the browser UI or FastAPI proxy to a phone/PC/Raspberry Pi. If FastAPI is mandatory as the deployed backend, use a companion host that proxies to the ESP32; do not attempt to run Python on the device. If SoftAP credentials or authentication provisioning is impractical, expose dashboard access only through serial-configured credentials and keep the AP disabled until explicitly enabled. If the existing NVS partition cannot support two records, use a dedicated data partition after verifying the flash layout; never replace atomic persistence with a single unprotected blob. If no physical machine is available for commissioning tests, use a temporary test-only simulator or injected fixture, verify that the production build has simulation disabled, and do not activate the resulting synthetic baseline for anomaly alerts.

AI

Updated implementation plan

Because the selected dashboard is device-hosted, FastAPI cannot run directly on the ESP32-C3. The implementation will use:

  • ESP-IDF native HTTP server on the ESP32-C3
  • Embedded lightweight HTML/JavaScript dashboard
  • REST endpoints for telemetry and commissioning commands
  • Optional FastAPI reference/proxy application for development on a PC later

The ESP32 will remain the production dashboard host.

Phase 2 — Commissioning and anomaly detection

Complete the existing control path:

  • Keep serial commands:

- STARTBASELINE - STOPBASELINE - RESETBASELINE - BASELINESTATUS - HELP

  • Route serial and dashboard commands through the same bounded command bus.
  • Require 10 complete cycles:
OFF → STARTING → RUNNING → STOPPING → OFF
  • Track per-phase:

- RMS mean/min/max/standard deviation - Peak statistics - Valid-window counts - Error and invalidation counters

  • Preserve the previous valid baseline during a new trial.
  • Store validated baselines in versioned, CRC-protected, two-slot NVS storage.
  • Derive thresholds:
warning  = max(0.08 g, mean + 3σ)
critical = max(0.30 g, mean + 5σ)
  • Enable anomaly detection only during RUNNING.
  • Require:

- 2 seconds above threshold to trigger - 5 seconds below recovery threshold to clear - 5-minute alert reminder interval

Phase 3 — LED alerts

Use the existing WS2812 LED on GPIO8:

  • Off: machine OFF
  • Blue: STARTING/STOPPING
  • Green: normal RUNNING
  • Yellow: baseline collection
  • Amber: warning
  • Red: critical anomaly
  • Purple: sensor fault

Priority:

  1. Sensor fault
  2. Critical anomaly
  3. Warning
  4. Baseline collection
  5. Operating phase

Device-hosted dashboard

Add an ESP-IDF HTTP server with:

  • Local WPA2 SoftAP
  • Device-derived SSID
  • Generated credentials
  • Authenticated state-changing requests
  • Dashboard polling at 1 Hz
  • Bounded in-memory history of approximately 120 telemetry points

Proposed endpoints:

GET  /                  Dashboard page
GET  /api/status        Current device and sensor state
GET  /api/history       Recent telemetry
GET  /api/baseline      Baseline status and thresholds
POST /api/baseline/start
POST /api/baseline/stop
POST /api/baseline/reset
POST /api/command       Shared command interface

The browser will display:

  • Current phase
  • Vibration RMS and peak
  • Temperature
  • Baseline progress
  • Warning/critical thresholds
  • Anomaly state
  • Recent telemetry chart
  • Sensor health
  • Commissioning controls

The dashboard will not modify GPIO assignments:

  • I²C SDA: GPIO4
  • I²C SCL: GPIO5
  • WS2812 LED: GPIO8

Validation

Before final documentation:

  • Build and syntax-check firmware.
  • Verify serial commands.
  • Verify dashboard endpoints and authentication.
  • Test interrupted baseline collection.
  • Test NVS recovery across reboot.
  • Test LED priority behavior.
  • Verify acquisition remains stable at 200 Hz.
  • Leave production configuration in real-sensor mode with simulation disabled.

FastAPI will be documented as an optional host-side reference/proxy, not deployed on the ESP32-C3.

include($ENV{IDF_PATH}/tools/cmake/project.cmake)
# "Trim" the build. Include the minimal set of components, main, and anything it depends on.

        default "mypassword"

        default 1
        help

    config ESP_MAX_STA_CONN

        range 60 65535

/* The examples use WiFi configuration that you can set via project configuration menu.

   If you'd rather not, just change the below entries to strings with
   the config you want - ie #define EXAMPLE_WIFI_SSID "mywifissid"
*/
#define EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_SSID      CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_SSID
#define EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_PASS      CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_PASSWORD
#define EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_CHANNEL   CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_CHANNEL
#define EXAMPLE_MAX_STA_CONN       CONFIG_ESP_MAX_STA_CONN

#if CONFIG_ESP_GTK_REKEYING_ENABLE
#define EXAMPLE_GTK_REKEY_INTERVAL CONFIG_ESP_GTK_REKEY_INTERVAL
#else
#define EXAMPLE_GTK_REKEY_INTERVAL 0
#endif

static const char *TAG = "wifi softAP";

static void wifi_event_handler(void* arg, esp_event_base_t event_base,
                                    int32_t event_id, void* event_data)
{
    if (event_id == WIFI_EVENT_AP_STACONNECTED) {
        wifi_event_ap_staconnected_t* event = (wifi_event_ap_staconnected_t*) event_data;
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "station "MACSTR" join, AID=%d",
                 MAC2STR(event->mac), event->aid);
    } else if (event_id == WIFI_EVENT_AP_STADISCONNECTED) {
        wifi_event_ap_stadisconnected_t* event = (wifi_event_ap_stadisconnected_t*) event_data;
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "station "MACSTR" leave, AID=%d, reason=%d",
                 MAC2STR(event->mac), event->aid, event->reason);
    }
}

void wifi_init_softap(void)
{
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_netif_init());
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_event_loop_create_default());
    esp_netif_create_default_wifi_ap();

    wifi_init_config_t cfg = WIFI_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_init(&cfg));

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_event_handler_instance_register(WIFI_EVENT,
                                                        ESP_EVENT_ANY_ID,
                                                        &wifi_event_handler,
                                                        NULL,
                                                        NULL));

    wifi_config_t wifi_config = {
        .ap = {
            .ssid = EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_SSID,
            .ssid_len = strlen(EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_SSID),
            .channel = EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_CHANNEL,
            .password = EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_PASS,
            .max_connection = EXAMPLE_MAX_STA_CONN,
#ifdef CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_SOFTAP_SAE_SUPPORT
            .authmode = WIFI_AUTH_WPA3_PSK,
            .sae_pwe_h2e = WPA3_SAE_PWE_BOTH,
#else /* CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_SOFTAP_SAE_SUPPORT */
            .authmode = WIFI_AUTH_WPA2_PSK,
#endif
            .pmf_cfg = {
                    .required = true,
            },
#ifdef CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_BSS_MAX_IDLE_SUPPORT
            .bss_max_idle_cfg = {
                .period = WIFI_AP_DEFAULT_MAX_IDLE_PERIOD,
                .protected_keep_alive = 1,
            },
#endif
            .gtk_rekey_interval = EXAMPLE_GTK_REKEY_INTERVAL,
        },
    };
    if (strlen(EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_PASS) == 0) {
        wifi_config.ap.authmode = WIFI_AUTH_OPEN;
    }

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_mode(WIFI_MODE_AP));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_config(WIFI_IF_AP, &wifi_config));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_start());

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "wifi_init_softap finished. SSID:%s password:%s channel:%d",
             EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_SSID, EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_PASS, EXAMPLE_ESP_WIFI_CHANNEL);
}

void app_main(void)
{
    //Initialize NVS
    esp_err_t ret = nvs_flash_init();
    if (ret == ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES || ret == ESP_ERR_NVS_NEW_VERSION_FOUND) {
      ESP_ERROR_CHECK(nvs_flash_erase());
      ret = nvs_flash_init();
    }
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(ret);

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "ESP_WIFI_MODE_AP");
    wifi_init_softap();
}

#include "sdkconfig.h"

#define MDNS_INSTANCE "esp home web server"

static const char *TAG = "example";

esp_err_t start_rest_server(const char *base_path);

static void initialise_mdns(void)
{
    mdns_init();
    mdns_hostname_set(CONFIG_EXAMPLE_MDNS_HOST_NAME);
    mdns_instance_name_set(MDNS_INSTANCE);

    mdns_txt_item_t serviceTxtData[] = {
        {"board", "esp32"},
        {"path", "/"}
    };

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(mdns_service_add("ESP32-WebServer", "_http", "_tcp", 80, serviceTxtData,
                                     sizeof(serviceTxtData) / sizeof(serviceTxtData[0])));
}

#if CONFIG_EXAMPLE_WEB_DEPLOY_SEMIHOST
esp_err_t init_fs(void)
{
    esp_err_t ret = esp_vfs_semihost_register(CONFIG_EXAMPLE_WEB_MOUNT_POINT);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to register semihost driver (%s)!", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    return ESP_OK;
}
#endif

#if CONFIG_EXAMPLE_WEB_DEPLOY_SD
esp_err_t init_fs(void)
{
    sdmmc_host_t host = SDMMC_HOST_DEFAULT();
    sdmmc_slot_config_t slot_config = SDMMC_SLOT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();

    gpio_set_pull_mode(15, GPIO_PULLUP_ONLY); // CMD
    gpio_set_pull_mode(2, GPIO_PULLUP_ONLY);  // D0
    gpio_set_pull_mode(4, GPIO_PULLUP_ONLY);  // D1
    gpio_set_pull_mode(12, GPIO_PULLUP_ONLY); // D2
    gpio_set_pull_mode(13, GPIO_PULLUP_ONLY); // D3

    esp_vfs_fat_sdmmc_mount_config_t mount_config = {
        .format_if_mount_failed = true,
        .max_files = 4,
        .allocation_unit_size = 16 * 1024
    };

    sdmmc_card_t *card;
    esp_err_t ret = esp_vfs_fat_sdmmc_mount(CONFIG_EXAMPLE_WEB_MOUNT_POINT, &host, &slot_config, &mount_config, &card);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        if (ret == ESP_FAIL) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to mount filesystem.");
        } else {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to initialize the card (%s)", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        }
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    /* print card info if mount successfully */
    sdmmc_card_print_info(stdout, card);
    return ESP_OK;
}
#endif

#if CONFIG_EXAMPLE_WEB_DEPLOY_SF
esp_err_t init_fs(void)
{
    esp_vfs_spiffs_conf_t conf = {
        .base_path = CONFIG_EXAMPLE_WEB_MOUNT_POINT,
        .partition_label = NULL,
        .max_files = 5,
        .format_if_mount_failed = false
    };
    esp_err_t ret = esp_vfs_spiffs_register(&conf);

    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        if (ret == ESP_FAIL) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to mount or format filesystem");
        } else if (ret == ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to find SPIFFS partition");
        } else {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to initialize SPIFFS (%s)", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        }
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }

    size_t total = 0, used = 0;
    ret = esp_spiffs_info(NULL, &total, &used);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to get SPIFFS partition information (%s)", esp_err_to_name(ret));
    } else {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Partition size: total: %d, used: %d", total, used);
    }
    return ESP_OK;
}
#endif

/* HTTP Restful API Server

   This example code is in the Public Domain (or CC0 licensed, at your option.)

   Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, this
   software is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR
   CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
*/
#include <string.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include "esp_http_server.h"
#include "esp_chip_info.h"
#include "esp_random.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "esp_vfs.h"
#include "cJSON.h"

static const char *REST_TAG = "esp-rest";
#define REST_CHECK(a, str, goto_tag, ...)                                              \
    do                                                                                 \
    {                                                                                  \
        if (!(a))                                                                      \
        {                                                                              \
            ESP_LOGE(REST_TAG, "%s(%d): " str, __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, ##__VA_ARGS__); \
            goto goto_tag;                                                             \
        }                                                                              \
    } while (0)

#define FILE_PATH_MAX (ESP_VFS_PATH_MAX + 128)
#define SCRATCH_BUFSIZE (10240)

typedef struct rest_server_context {
    char base_path[ESP_VFS_PATH_MAX + 1];
    char scratch[SCRATCH_BUFSIZE];
} rest_server_context_t;

#define CHECK_FILE_EXTENSION(filename, ext) (strcasecmp(&filename[strlen(filename) - strlen(ext)], ext) == 0)

/* Set HTTP response content type according to file extension */
static esp_err_t set_content_type_from_file(httpd_req_t *req, const char *filepath)
{
    const char *type = "text/plain";
    if (CHECK_FILE_EXTENSION(filepath, ".html")) {
        type = "text/html";
    } else if (CHECK_FILE_EXTENSION(filepath, ".js")) {
        type = "application/javascript";
    } else if (CHECK_FILE_EXTENSION(filepath, ".css")) {
        type = "text/css";
    } else if (CHECK_FILE_EXTENSION(filepath, ".png")) {
        type = "image/png";
    } else if (CHECK_FILE_EXTENSION(filepath, ".ico")) {
        type = "image/x-icon";
    } else if (CHECK_FILE_EXTENSION(filepath, ".svg")) {
        type = "text/xml";
    }
    return httpd_resp_set_type(req, type);
}

/* Send HTTP response with the contents of the requested file */
static esp_err_t rest_common_get_handler(httpd_req_t *req)
{
    char filepath[FILE_PATH_MAX];

    rest_server_context_t *rest_context = (rest_server_context_t *)req->user_ctx;
    strlcpy(filepath, rest_context->base_path, sizeof(filepath));
    if (req->uri[strlen(req->uri) - 1] == '/') {
        strlcat(filepath, "/index.html", sizeof(filepath));
    } else {
        strlcat(filepath, req->uri, sizeof(filepath));
    }
    int fd = open(filepath, O_RDONLY, 0);
    if (fd == -1) {
        ESP_LOGE(REST_TAG, "Failed to open file : %s", filepath);
        /* Respond with 500 Internal Server Error */
        httpd_resp_send_err(req, HTTPD_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "Failed to read existing file");
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }

    set_content_type_from_file(req, filepath);

    char *chunk = rest_context->scratch;
    ssize_t read_bytes;
    do {
        /* Read file in chunks into the scratch buffer */
        read_bytes = read(fd, chunk, SCRATCH_BUFSIZE);
        if (read_bytes == -1) {
            ESP_LOGE(REST_TAG, "Failed to read file : %s", filepath);
        } else if (read_bytes > 0) {
            /* Send the buffer contents as HTTP response chunk */
            if (httpd_resp_send_chunk(req, chunk, read_bytes) != ESP_OK) {
                close(fd);
                ESP_LOGE(REST_TAG, "File sending failed!");
                /* Abort sending file */
                httpd_resp_sendstr_chunk(req, NULL);
                /* Respond with 500 Internal Server Error */
                httpd_resp_send_err(req, HTTPD_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "Failed to send file");
                return ESP_FAIL;
            }
        }
    } while (read_bytes > 0);
    /* Close file after sending complete */
    close(fd);
    ESP_LOGI(REST_TAG, "File sending complete");
    /* Respond with an empty chunk to signal HTTP response completion */
    httpd_resp_send_chunk(req, NULL, 0);
    return ESP_OK;
}

/* Simple handler for light brightness control */
static esp_err_t light_brightness_post_handler(httpd_req_t *req)
{
    int total_len = req->content_len;
    int cur_len = 0;
    char *buf = ((rest_server_context_t *)(req->user_ctx))->scratch;
    int received = 0;
    if (total_len >= SCRATCH_BUFSIZE) {
        /* Respond with 500 Internal Server Error */
        httpd_resp_send_err(req, HTTPD_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "content too long");
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    while (cur_len < total_len) {
        received = httpd_req_recv(req, buf + cur_len, total_len);
        if (received <= 0) {
            /* Respond with 500 Internal Server Error */
            httpd_resp_send_err(req, HTTPD_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "Failed to post control value");
            return ESP_FAIL;
        }
        cur_len += received;
    }
    buf[total_len] = '\0';

    cJSON *root = cJSON_Parse(buf);
    int red = cJSON_GetObjectItem(root, "red")->valueint;
    int green = cJSON_GetObjectItem(root, "green")->valueint;
    int blue = cJSON_GetObjectItem(root, "blue")->valueint;
    ESP_LOGI(REST_TAG, "Light control: red = %d, green = %d, blue = %d", red, green, blue);
    cJSON_Delete(root);
    httpd_resp_sendstr(req, "Post control value successfully");
    return ESP_OK;
}

/* Simple handler for getting system handler */
static esp_err_t system_info_get_handler(httpd_req_t *req)
{
    httpd_resp_set_type(req, "application/json");
    cJSON *root = cJSON_CreateObject();
    esp_chip_info_t chip_info;
    esp_chip_info(&chip_info);
    cJSON_AddStringToObject(root, "version", IDF_VER);
    cJSON_AddNumberToObject(root, "cores", chip_info.cores);
    const char *sys_info = cJSON_Print(root);
    httpd_resp_sendstr(req, sys_info);
    free((void *)sys_info);
    cJSON_Delete(root);
    return ESP_OK;
}

/* Simple handler for getting temperature data */
static esp_err_t temperature_data_get_handler(httpd_req_t *req)
{
    httpd_resp_set_type(req, "application/json");
    cJSON *root = cJSON_CreateObject();
    cJSON_AddNumberToObject(root, "raw", esp_random() % 20);
    const char *sys_info = cJSON_Print(root);
    httpd_resp_sendstr(req, sys_info);
    free((void *)sys_info);
    cJSON_Delete(root);
    return ESP_OK;
}

esp_err_t start_rest_server(const char *base_path)
{
    REST_CHECK(base_path, "wrong base path", err);
    rest_server_context_t *rest_context = calloc(1, sizeof(rest_server_context_t));
    REST_CHECK(rest_context, "No memory for rest context", err);
    strlcpy(rest_context->base_path, base_path, sizeof(rest_context->base_path));

    httpd_handle_t server = NULL;
    httpd_config_t config = HTTPD_DEFAULT_CONFIG();
    config.uri_match_fn = httpd_uri_match_wildcard;

    ESP_LOGI(REST_TAG, "Starting HTTP Server");
    REST_CHECK(httpd_start(&server, &config) == ESP_OK, "Start server failed", err_start);

    /* URI handler for fetching system info */
    httpd_uri_t system_info_get_uri = {
        .uri = "/api/v1/system/info",
        .method = HTTP_GET,
        .handler = system_info_get_handler,
        .user_ctx = rest_context
    };
    httpd_register_uri_handler(server, &system_info_get_uri);

    /* URI handler for fetching temperature data */
    httpd_uri_t temperature_data_get_uri = {
        .uri = "/api/v1/temp/raw",
        .method = HTTP_GET,
        .handler = temperature_data_get_handler,
        .user_ctx = rest_context
    };
    httpd_register_uri_handler(server, &temperature_data_get_uri);

    /* URI handler for light brightness control */
    httpd_uri_t light_brightness_post_uri = {
        .uri = "/api/v1/light/brightness",
        .method = HTTP_POST,
        .handler = light_brightness_post_handler,
        .user_ctx = rest_context
    };
    httpd_register_uri_handler(server, &light_brightness_post_uri);

    /* URI handler for getting web server files */
    httpd_uri_t common_get_uri = {
        .uri = "/*",
        .method = HTTP_GET,
        .handler = rest_common_get_handler,
        .user_ctx = rest_context
    };
    httpd_register_uri_handler(server, &common_get_uri);

    return ESP_OK;
err_start:
    free(rest_context);
err:
    return ESP_FAIL;
}
